lots.working: Maximum bids need a same-item SOLD sale within 24 months. None found: no other 'Hamilton' impression traced. The only close comparable (Nocturne litho, $400) is 26 months old; the in-window entries are a reproduction print and a large-edition screen print, both category guides. So keep_max_hammer = 0 and flip_max_hammer = 0. lots.confidence_reason: Signature 'G. Callaghan 83' and 'Hamilton 7/7' read clearly in the photos, but there is no same-print SOLD evidence, the one close comparable is outside the window, and medium (lithograph versus other print process) is inferred from the image texture, not confirmed.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 2: pencil signature 'G. Callaghan 83' in the lower margin. Photo 3: pencil title 'Hamilton' and edition '7/7' lower left, with faint artist's title also in the image corner. Photo 4: crayon-like grained texture consistent with a lithograph. Photo 2 also shows tide marks and foxing spots on the cream mat; the sheet margin looks toned. Frame plain, appears sound.
lots.condition: Mat water-stained and foxed (visible tide lines in photo 2); paper margins toned; image itself appears clean from photos; frame sound. Possible staining under the mat not visible.
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped as not comparable (original works, not prints): Lawsons 'Flautist' pastel $200 (2024-09-03); Colville 2022 watercolours and oils $200-400; Colville 2022 passed-in watercolour and oil (UNSOLD, last bids 100 and 200), all opened on the Invaluable artist page and confirmed, but originals and over 24 months old. The researcher's direct Invaluable lot URL for Nocturne returned an empty page to curl, so that entry rests on the artist page instead. WebSearch budget was exhausted, so no further Armitage, Leonard Joel or Theodore Bruce searches were possible.
lots.question_for_armitage: Can you check whether the print has any staining or foxing under the mat on the sheet itself, whether it is a lithograph, etching or other print (any blind stamp or printer's mark), and the sight size? Is there any gallery label on the back?
